title: Tentacle Robotic Gripper
summary: From hyperelastic simulation to a soft robotic prototype.
team: Ayoub Hamam, Julian Meskens, Matteo Paolini, Ariadne Samaey & Henri Wauthier
overview: A pneumatic soft gripper designed by our team to handle delicate, irregular objects. Four silicone tentacles deform around the object, integrated with a two-degree-of-freedom arm.
constraints: The design had to balance compliant bending, wall integrity, fabrication and integration. A 200 g payload was a project requirement, not a verified maximum load.
contribution: I worked on the hyperelastic finite-element analysis of the silicone actuator, designed the casting mold and 3D-printed the tooling. The arm, electronics and integrated system were team work.
approach: The actuator geometry was investigated in simulation before tooling. Mold design connected the internal chamber geometry to a casting process and a removable core.
results: The team published a build guide and a prototype demonstration. The demo documents the integrated system; it does not by itself quantify agreement between the FEM model and measurements.
limits: The team documented shoulder rigidity, custom-belt reliability and the absence of active pump regulation as limitations. Quantitative model validation is a separate question.
